reasons: The cited clause fails the fallback on every material term: it is one-way (binds only Customer), is a true no-hire ('solicit, hire, or employ'), covers all Vendor employees rather than only personnel involved in the Services, runs 24 months post-term, and expressly negates any general-advertising/unsolicited-application carve-out — squarely in walk-away territory, so 'deviation' is the correct classification and not over-flagging.

The redline (deletion of Section 12.4) reaches the preferred position ('No non-solicit on Customer') and matches the rule's redline guidance to delete any no-hire; deleting a wholly walk-away one-way clause is the appropriate minimal edit rather than rewriting it, and it also removes the internal contradiction with Section 12.3.

The comment is accurate, concise, in-tone, prefixed correctly, explains what changed and why, and offers the sensible fallback (mutual, involved personnel only, 12 months post-involvement, with general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs).

The failed deterministic checks ('duration ≤ 12 months', 'general-solicitation carve-out present') are artefacts of a full deletion — no duration or carve-out text can remain — and do not indicate a defective edit.
Escalated to high because the clause sits in explicit walk-away territory (no-hire covering all Vendor personnel for 24 months).
